The build passes regardless.

```go
mx1 := xStep(y2, x2, y3, x3)      // short edge y2→y3
mx2 := xStep(y1, x1, y3, x3)      // long edge y1→y3
sx1 := x2
sx2 := x1 + xStep(y1, x1, y3, x3)*(y2-y1)
```

The duplicate dead assignments are gone. Edge slopes are consistent with their start points. Correct.

✅ **VERIFIED.** The `collides` function directly enters the AABB triple-loop with no dead conditional wrapper. Clean.

✅ **VERIFIED (partially).** The `castRay()` wrapper method no longer exists. Only `castRayInternal()` remains, called by both left-click and right-click handlers. The functional goal (single method) is achieved; the rename is cosmetic only and has no effect on correctness.

```go
px, py, pz := int(math.Floor(g.Player.X)), int(math.Floor(g.Player.Y+1.0)), int(math.Floor(g.Player.Z))
for dy := 0; dy < 2; dy++ {
    if placedX == px && placedY == py+dy && placedZ == pz { insidePlayer = true }
}
```
The builder's claimed AABB-based check was not written to disk. This leaves a low-severity false-negative risk (placing a block inside the player's 0.3×1.8 collision box when adjacent).

✅ **VERIFIED.** `UnloadFarChunks(cx, cz, radius int)` exists in `world/world.go`. Called in `main.go` `Update()` with `g.UnloadDist = 10`. Stale mesh cleanup loop also present. Correctly prevents memory leak.
